messages:
sasha: Heads-up — trying to onboard a HF model that requires trust_remote_code and a custom config class. Redwood conversion crashes on tokenizer and chat template mapping. Anyone seen this?

aj: Yep. Usually the HF repo uses a custom Tokenizer/Config that lives behind trust_remote_code. Did you run AutoTokenizer/AutoConfig with trust_remote_code=True during conversion?

sasha: I did that locally: `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True)` but our rwd conversion step fails with `auto_map` mismatch: "architecture not found in auto_map". The model's config.json has an `auto_map` entry pointing to a custom class path.

oliver: Can you paste the top of config.json? Often auto_map points to something like `{'AutoModel': 'repo.custom.modeling.CustomModel'}` which our shim doesn't handle.

sasha: ```json
{"architectures":["CustomModel"],
 "auto_map": {"AutoModelForCausalLM": "repo.custom.modeling.CustomCausal"},
 "tokenizer_class": "repo.custom.tokenization.CustomTokenizer",
 "eos_token_id": 2}
```

kevin: OK, two separate issues: (1) tokenizers that are custom require executing remote code to instantiate; (2) auto_map entries mean the conversion needs a mapping/shim so our runtime knows the correct architecture -> Redwood Model class.

maria: Quant note: I ran int8 quant on a copy and saw a small quality regression on our chat eval (drop in ROUGE ~3 points and a few template failures). The template failures are because the tokenizer's special tokens differ (eos/pad). After quant, decode behavior changed when special_tokens_map wasn't applied.

aj: Quick workaround: download tokenizer files from HF repo (vocab.json, merges.txt, special_tokens_map.json, tokenizer_config.json) and pass them directly to the conversion step so we avoid importing the custom tokenizer class. Example: `rwd convert --tokenizer-path ./tokenizer_files --model-dir ./hf`

sasha: Tried that, but the tokenizer_config had a reference to the custom class name and the conversion script still attempted to import it. We need the converter to ignore `tokenizer_class` if files are present.

oliver: I can add a small shim: if `special_tokens_map.json` exists then force a PlainTokenizer wrapper and populate special tokens from the file. That should unblock chat template alignment.

kevin: Also add a hook to normalize `eos_token_id` vs `sep_token_id` in our template loader: some custom tokenizers use different ids but same strings, and quantized kernels pick the first occurance leading to off-by-one decoding.

ml-onboard: For trust_remote_code models we should: (1) add `--allow-remote-code` flag to converter (logs it and warns), (2) fallback to static tokenizer files if importer fails, (3) emit a QA ticket to run evals pre/post quant. I'll draft a checklist.

ci-bot: CI: convert-cases (linux-ubuntu-22) failed for job 412 with exit code 1 — see logs: https://ci.redwood/inference/412/logs

maria: I'll rerun the quant baseline after the tokenizer shim. I have the eval prompt set and will attach the diff. If regressed >2% we'll pin to FP16 for now.

aj: For the auto_map issue: create a small mapping config in our conversion layer where `repo.custom.modeling.CustomCausal` -> `redwood.runtime.models.GenericCausalAdapter` and include a test that instantiates parameters shape-only (no forward) to sanity check.

sasha: I've opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/523 — adds `--allow-remote-code`, tokenizer-file fallback, and an auto_map shim + test. PTAL.

kevin: Reviewed, left two nits about logging and a unit for special_tokens_map absent case. Otherwise :thumbsup:

oliver: I'll follow up and add the eos/sep normalization in a separate patch.

sasha: Plan: (a) CI logs -> attach artifacts, (b) ml-onboard run quant baseline after shim, (c) if regressions persist open model-quality incident. Thanks all. :pray:
